## THE NOBEL PRIZE IN CHEMISTRY

A 1986 DNA model used by Aziz Sancar, who was awarded the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

Some molecules, such as amino acids, exist as two variants that are each other’s mirror image. However, living organisms only contain one of these mirror images. How chemical asymmetry such as this could have emerged was long a mystery to chemists. Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 for discovering a solution to this puzzle.

[Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/)[Popular information: They solved chemistry’s asymmetric mystery](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/popular-information/)

[Scientific background: Non-linear effects and auto catalysis in asymmetric organic catalysis](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/advanced-information/)

[Prize announcement](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/prize-announcement/)

[![Image 1: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 to [Henri B. Kagan](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/kagan/facts/) and [Kenso Soai](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/soai/facts/) “for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.”

Henri Kagan discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions, allowing a greater excess of one of the mirror images to be created than was previously assumed possible. His discovery has been revolutionary for chemists who develop reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, flavours, scents and new materials.

Kenso Soai designed the first chemical reaction in which only one of the potential mirror images was formed. Other than life itself, no one had ever achieved this feat. The _Soai reaction_ is one of the most spectacular chemical experiments ever conducted.

[![Image 2: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/summary/)

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

> “Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have provided a solution to a chemical mystery that is over a century old: how homochirality can emerge spontaneously. The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular.”
> 
> Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry

Did you know that some chemical reactions create two different molecules, which are mirror images of each other?

Chemistry prize 2021

### [Ernest Rutherford](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1908/rutherford/ "Ernest Rutherford")

[Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1908](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1908/rutherford/)for his investigations into the disintegration of the elements, and the chemistry of radioactive substances.

[![Image 10: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/)

### [Marie Curie, née Skłodowska](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/ "Marie Curie, née Skłodowska")

[Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1911/marie-curie/)in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element.

[Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/)in recognition of the extraordinary services they have rendered by their joint researches on the radiation phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel.

[![Image 11: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1964/hodgkin/)

### [Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1964/hodgkin/ "Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin")

[Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1964](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1964/hodgkin/)for her determinations by X-ray techniques of the structures of important biochemical substances.

[![Image 12: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2016/sauvage/)

### [Jean-Pierre Sauvage](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2016/sauvage/ "Jean-Pierre Sauvage")

[Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2016](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2016/sauvage/)for the design and synthesis of molecular machines.

[![Image 13: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2011/shechtman/)[![Image 14: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2018/arnold/)

Learn more about Svante Arrhenius, who first made the connection between carbon dioxide levels and global temperature.

[![Image 15: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1903/arrhenius/biographical/)

Credit: NASA

Watch the Nobel Lecture by one of 2016’s laureates Jean-Pierre Sauvage, who helped develop molecular machines.

[![Image 16: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/mediaplayer?id=2678)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

### [Interview with a double awardee](https://www.nobelprize.org/mediaplayer?id=360)

Frederick Sanger received the prize twice: in 1958 for his work on the structure of proteins and in 1980 for DNA sequencing.

[![Image 17: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/mediaplayer?id=360)

The double Nobel-awarded laureate Frederick Sanger‘s calibration catalogue of amino acids

© Nobel Media. Photo: Alexander Mahmoud

Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1964

### [Mapping molecules](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/women-who-changed-science/dorothy-hodgkin/)

Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin’s work determining the 3D structure of molecules had immediate implications. Her map of the structure of penicillin made the drug easier to manufacture.

[![Image 18: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/women-who-changed-science/dorothy-hodgkin/)

Photo: Science Museum London/Science and Society Picture Library [CC BY-SA 2.0], via Wikimedia Commons

Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1961

### [Carbon dioxide assimilation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1961/calvin/lecture/)

Melvin Calvin showed how plants convert carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and created a clear picture of a complicated sequence of reactions.

[![Image 19: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1961/calvin/lecture/)

Berkeley Labs

Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2018

### [Enzyme revolution](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/women-who-changed-science/frances-arnold/)

Frances Arnold conducted the first directed evolution of enzymes. The uses of results include more environmentally friendly manufacturing of chemical substances.

[![Image 20: Chemistry Laureate Frances Arnold in the laboratory](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/stories/women-who-changed-science/frances-arnold/)
